title: Official Hyperliquid annual ecosystem event
access_note: Invite-only; reported cap of 200 C-suite and department heads
summary: Hyperliquid’s own annual ecosystem event opening TOKEN week. Reported as invite-only and capped at 200 C-suite and department heads, with doors 09:00–17:00 and a speaking agenda from 15:00 to 17:00.
why: Hyperliquid (through HIP-4) is trying to make outcome markets a permissionless building block that other teams can deploy, rather than a single-company product. This is the ecosystem's own opening event of the week.
questions: What new outcome-market deployments will be live by Singapore?
Who is actually supplying liquidity to third-party HIP-4 markets?
status_note: Date from Hyperliquid’s announcement; time, format and cap as reported by Hype Global on a page that is now offline. Venue still not published.
clash_note: Overlaps the start of Haruko x Kalshi (from 17:00) only if the event runs late.

title: More than a million, Haruko x Kalshi
venue: Downtown Core (exact address shared after approval)
summary: Invite-only opening-week gathering hosted around Haruko and Kalshi participants.
why: Haruko connects prediction-market and derivatives exposure to institutional portfolio and risk systems, and has announced a Kalshi integration. Expect people working on the institutional plumbing. Note: the integration is documented; how widely institutions use it is not.
questions: Who is actually carrying prediction-market positions inside institutional portfolio systems?
What changes operationally when event-contract exposure sits beside crypto or derivatives books?
status_note: Listed on a side-event directory; company pages support the Haruko–Kalshi relationship.
clash_note: May clash with the official Hyperliquid ecosystem event once its time is published.

title: Hyperliquid Forum Singapore
summary: Full-day institutional Hyperliquid forum, run by DAYS as part of the Digital Asset Yield Summit and reported as co-hosted by Grayscale. Its six themes include custody, liquidity and execution, capital efficiency, tokenised markets, and prediction and outcome markets.
why: The clearest place to see what happens when outcome markets become infrastructure that other teams can deploy (Hyperliquid's HIP-4). Listed participants include people from DoubleZero, Outcome, Outcome Labs and Selini.
questions: What exactly is live under HIP-4 now?
What is still subsidised or incentive-driven?
How do settlement responsibility and liquidity work across third-party builders?
status_note: Organiser page. Hyperliquid's SEC filing and announcements provide HIP-4 context.
clash_note: Runs alongside the Digital Asset Yield Summit at the same venue.

title: Digital Asset Yield Summit
summary: Institutional digital-asset income event running in conjunction with the Hyperliquid Forum.
why: Not a prediction-market event. Relevant where allocators, market makers or infrastructure firms overlap with prediction-market questions. Easy to combine with the Hyperliquid Forum.
questions: Do institutional allocators see event contracts as a trade, a hedge, or a separate product bucket?
status_note: Organiser page (DAYS). Also listed on the Hyperliquid Forum page.

title: The Institutional Ark by ChainUp
summary: Institutional evening for executives, allocators and infrastructure firms, hosted by ChainUp.
why: ChainUp sells Hermes, white-label prediction-market software that claims shared liquidity. The room is likely to include businesses considering launching their own prediction market. Hermes claims are the company's own and have not been independently tested.
questions: Show me where liquidity actually originates in a new Hermes deployment.
What happens if upstream liquidity disappears?
Which controls and settlement responsibilities stay with the operator?
status_note: Organiser page.

title: Opening Bell: Zenith, Kaiko & T-REX
summary: Institutional breakfast focused on digital-asset market structure, tokenisation and settlement.
why: Kaiko's involvement makes it relevant to the market-data layer. It overlaps the Polymarket main-stage fireside.
questions: What would a professional prediction-market data product need that current exchange feeds do not provide?
status_note: Organiser page. End time not published.
clash_note: Likely overlaps the 09:30 Polymarket fireside on the OKX Main Stage. The breakfast's end time isn't published, so this can't be calculated.

title: ChainUp at TOKEN2049 (booth PB4-8)
summary: ChainUp is a TOKEN2049 Gold sponsor exhibiting its enterprise infrastructure suite, which explicitly includes prediction markets.
why: The practical place to see a demo of Hermes, its white-label prediction-market product, and ask how market creation, settlement and liquidity routing work.
questions: Can you demonstrate market creation, settlement and liquidity routing live?
Which prediction-market customers or pilots can be discussed on the record?
status_note: Sponsorship on the official TOKEN2049 partners page; booth number from ChainUp.

title: Predict.fun at TOKEN2049 (Gold sponsor)
summary: Predict.fun is listed as a TOKEN2049 Gold sponsor. Its recent announcements cover Chainlink-based market lifecycle and settlement, and block trading of 100,000+ shares with liquidity from Susquehanna Crypto.
why: One prediction-market company that touches oracle/lifecycle automation, professional liquidity and block execution, which makes it a compact way to see several layers of the stack. These details are company claims.
questions: Who is using the 100k+ share block service?
What remains manual in market creation and settlement?
How much liquidity is organic versus supported by professional counterparties?
status_note: Gold sponsorship on the official TOKEN2049 partners page. Booth location not recorded.

title: Polymarket Fireside Chat: Shayne Coplan with Balaji Srinivasan
venue: OKX Main Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: TOKEN2049 flagship conversation centred on Polymarket, prediction-market growth and what comes next.
why: Polymarket on the main stage. Listen for how the company now defines itself (exchange, information network, media or consumer app) and where institutional participation fits.
questions: Does Polymarket describe itself as an exchange, information network, media product, consumer app or some combination?
What does it want to own versus outsource as the stack matures?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Market Wizards
summary: Trading and market-making session with Dim Selk and Jordi Alexander.
why: Market-making context. Useful for understanding which parts of crypto market making carry over to binary and multi-outcome contracts.
questions: What parts of crypto market making transfer cleanly into binary or multi-outcome contracts?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Building the Neobrokerage
summary: Brokerage and distribution discussion with Armani Ferrante and Kyle Samani.
why: Who owns the customer when new asset classes, prediction markets included, are embedded inside broader trading apps?
questions: Do prediction markets become a destination or simply another instrument inside a brokerage?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: DeFi’s Institutional Breakthrough
venue: OKX Main Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: Institutional DeFi panel with Stani Kulechov, Guy Young, Kain Warwick and Guy Wuollet.
why: A comparison point: how infrastructure changed once retail-native DeFi sought institutional capital. Prediction markets may now be going through the same transition.
questions: Which institutional controls emerged only after DeFi reached scale, and do PMs now face the same transition?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Wall St. 2049: Everything Trades, Nobody Sleeps
summary: Session built explicitly around an “everything is tradable” framing of markets.
why: Shows how TOKEN2049 is grouping prediction markets into a wider expansion of tradable outcomes and assets.
questions: What gets lost when every measurable outcome becomes framed as tradable?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Hyperliquid: Rebuilding Finance from First Principles
venue: OKX Main Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: Hyperliquid flagship session with Jeff Yan and Hart Lambur.
why: HIP-4 makes Hyperliquid directly relevant to permissionless outcome markets and shared-collateral infrastructure.
questions: Where do outcome markets sit in Hyperliquid’s long-term product architecture?
How much responsibility should be pushed to third-party builders?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: AI Agents Trading on the Blockchain
summary: Session on agentic trading.
why: Relevant if AI agents become prediction-market users, liquidity providers or autonomous participants.
questions: Are prediction markets especially suitable for autonomous agents because positions have bounded outcomes and explicit resolution rules?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Agentic Trading: Will AI Outperform Human Traders?
venue: Bit Digital Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: AI trading session with Alex Svanevik.
why: Another angle on AI agents as market participants, including how agents would read contract rules and settlement terms.
questions: Where would agents obtain reliable contract semantics and settlement rules?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Bringing Perps to America
summary: John Wang, Head of Crypto at Kalshi, on perpetuals and US market expansion.
why: Kalshi increasingly sits where event contracts meet broader derivatives. Separately, Kalshi Klear has been reported as requesting permission to margin event contracts for qualifying institutions. That is a request, not an approval.
questions: If institutional event contracts move from full collateralisation toward margin, what changes first in risk, clearing and participation?
Does Kalshi see event contracts and perps converging operationally?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Robinhood Chain
summary: Johann Kerbrat and Ran Neuner on Robinhood’s blockchain and distribution strategy.
why: Robinhood is central to whether prediction markets become a destination product or another asset inside a brokerage app.
questions: Who owns discovery and education when event contracts are embedded inside an existing brokerage?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Next Billion Users Should Never Touch Blockchain
venue: Bit Digital Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: A consumer and mainstreaming critique from Pauline Shangett.
why: An outsider's view on trust and user experience. Useful for thinking about what a prediction product must simplify before mainstream users trust it.
questions: What would a prediction product have to hide or simplify before mainstream users trust it?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: From the White House to Wall Street: What’s Next for Crypto?
summary: Policy and institutional session including Jake Chervinsky of the Hyperliquid Policy Center, with participants from Kraken, Paxos and Pantera.
why: Relevant to the regulatory boundary around permissionless financial products, including outcome markets.
questions: How should responsibility be divided between protocol, deployer and frontend when event contracts are permissionless?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Crypto’s Identity Crisis: What Are We Actually Betting On?
summary: Session on crypto’s market identity: speculation versus utility.
why: Framing material on where the line sits between useful risk transfer and pure speculation. Prediction markets sit right on that line.
questions: Where is the line between useful risk transfer and pure speculation in tokenised markets?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Tokenized Markets: How Institutional Finance Moves Onchain
summary: Andrew McCormick, Michael Higgins, Joshua Lim and Roland Chai discuss institutional finance moving onchain.
why: Joshua Lim (FalconX) is on the panel, and FalconX sits in the institutional-execution layer of the prediction-market stack. A good session for the question of what institutions need after execution access: clearing, risk, data or prime services.
questions: After execution access, what is the next bottleneck for institutional event contracts?
Which functions will be supplied by existing financial-market infrastructure rather than PM-native companies?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Perps x Institutional: Trading, Liquidity & the Onchain Economy
summary: Side event hosted by lil room covering perps, RWA, stablecoins, DeFi liquidity, AI and live trading.
why: Focused on perps rather than prediction markets. Relevant mainly as a gathering of market makers and execution specialists whose problems overlap with event contracts.
questions: Which execution problems in perps reappear in event contracts?
status_note: Organiser Luma page (host: lil room). Also listed on Dexpal, which gave a later finish (20:30); times here follow the Luma page.

title: Perp Traders Mixer @Token2049 Singapore
summary: Invite-only morning mixer hosted by HyprEarn for the Hyperliquid and perp-trading community, with panels and fireside chats on perpetuals. Aimed at perp traders, Hyperliquid-native funds, protocol teams, AI trading builders and VCs.
why: Not a prediction-market event and the page doesn't mention them. Relevant as a room of Hyperliquid-native traders and funds, the same crowd most likely to trade HIP-4 outcome markets.
questions: Are Hyperliquid perp traders already trading HIP-4 outcome markets, and what would make them size up?
status_note: Organiser Luma page. Venue not yet announced.

title: Polymarket Singapore Kick-Off
access_note: Invitation-only; full with a waitlist at the latest check
summary: Polymarket’s first exclusive Singapore event, publicly hosted by 528 Collective. Curated, and full with a waitlist at the latest check.
why: The main Wednesday-evening gathering for the Polymarket ecosystem: builders, traders and partners. Context: Singapore’s gambling regulator has blocked access to Polymarket since January 2025, so this is an ecosystem and networking event rather than a local product launch.
questions: What is being built around Polymarket that is not visible from the consumer frontend?
Which infrastructure, liquidity and distribution partners are becoming strategically important?
status_note: Organiser event page (Luma).

title: Zoomex Traders After Party @ TOKEN2049
summary: Traders’ after-party with a panel that explicitly spans derivatives, TradFi and prediction markets.
why: Prediction markets are named in the panel description, but this is a general traders’ party rather than a prediction-market event.
questions: Who on the panel actually trades prediction markets versus discussing them conceptually?
status_note: Organiser event page; corroborated by a Zoomex press release.

title: Ripple x Citadel Securities Sundown Mixer
summary: An invitation-only mixer involving Ripple and Citadel Securities that surfaced in earlier research. No first-party event page has been found.
why: Potentially relevant for institutional market-making conversations, but unconfirmed.
questions: Does Citadel Securities see event contracts as a distinct market-making problem or another derivative microstructure problem?
status_note: No first-party source found. Treat as unconfirmed.

title: The New Institutional Market: Tokenized Assets. Global Liquidity. Onchain Settlement
venue: OKX Main Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: Institutional tokenisation session with Jenny Johnson and Richard Teng.
why: How established finance thinks about tokenised infrastructure, settlement and global liquidity. A useful benchmark for prediction markets' own institutional push.
questions: Which parts of traditional post-trade infrastructure remain non-negotiable when new instruments move onchain?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: HypurrCo / HypurrCollective Gathers
venue: Bugis area (exact location shared close to the event)
summary: Curated Hyperliquid ecosystem brunch for builders, KOLs, market makers and top holders, presented with Hyperliquid Strategies, Hyperliquid Policy Center and Insilico Terminal. The page cites a maturing frontend ecosystem under HIP-4. Listed partners include Hyperliquid Policy Center, Insilico, Nansen, Chainlink, Wintermute, Tread.fi and 21Shares, among others.
why: A dense concentration of Hyperliquid, outcome-market and market-infrastructure companies in one room.
questions: Which PM/outcome products are actually live on Hyperliquid by this week?
Who is making the markets and who is subsidising liquidity?
What breaks if permissionless outcome deployment grows 10x?
status_note: Organiser Luma page and Telegram channel. Presented with Hyperliquid Strategies, Hyperliquid Policy Center and Insilico Terminal. Schedule not yet published.

title: HFT Closed-Door Meetup
summary: Closed-door trading, infrastructure and institutional meetup hosted by Quant Ferryman.
why: Not prediction-market-specific. Relevant if you care about latency, feed normalisation and inventory problems that also show up in event contracts.
questions: Which latency, feed-normalisation and inventory problems are genuinely different in event contracts?
status_note: Listed on a third-party side-event directory (Dexpal). Prediction-market participation not confirmed.

title: Austin Federa / DoubleZero keynote
venue: Marina Bay Sands (stage: check the TOKEN2049 app)
summary: Keynote from DoubleZero founder Austin Federa.
why: DoubleZero now carries Kalshi’s full order-book market data, which puts specialised low-latency networking inside the prediction-market stack.
questions: Why do prediction markets need purpose-built low-latency transport now?
Which users are consuming full order-book data over the network?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda. Stage not recorded.

title: Fireside Chat with Nasdaq CEO Adena Friedman
venue: OKX Main Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: Main-stage conversation on exchange infrastructure.
why: An outside benchmark for what mature exchange infrastructure, market integrity and distribution look like.
questions: Which functions must become boring before a new asset class becomes institutionally normal?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: The Future of Real World Assets: On Chain Equities, Perps, and Beyond
venue: OKX Main Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: Kyle Samani on the expansion of tradable onchain assets.
why: Frames the growing set of onchain instruments. Runs immediately before “The Speculation Age” on the same stage.
questions: Where do event contracts fit among the expanding set of onchain instruments?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: Institutional Crypto Capital Flows
summary: Institutional flow panel with CME, Coinbase Institutional and Invesco participants.
why: Relevant to whether event contracts would sit inside existing derivatives mandates or need separate treatment.
questions: Would event contracts sit inside existing derivatives mandates or need separate risk/governance treatment?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: The Speculation Age: When Everything Becomes Tradable
venue: OKX Main Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: Johann Kerbrat (Robinhood), Vladimir Novakovski (Lighter) and John Wang (Kalshi), moderated by Jordi Alexander.
why: The official session most directly about what prediction markets are becoming: a destination of their own, or one instrument inside an “everything-tradable” brokerage.
questions: Does the customer think in asset classes or simply opportunities?
Who owns discovery, liquidity and risk when everything is tradable in one interface?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 agenda.

title: The Odds: Prediction Markets Live
summary: A dedicated prediction-markets conference by More & More covering market structure, liquidity and regulation, with private meeting rooms and a partner/demo area. Co-hosted with Agentic Finance (a closed-door, invitation-only summit for about 400 senior decision-makers) at the same venue on the same day.
why: The biggest block of prediction-market-specific programming of the week, with particular depth on sports market structure and infrastructure. The co-located Agentic Finance audience adds finance, compliance and media people.
questions: What sports-book infrastructure transfers into prediction markets and what does not?
Who pays for official data and who carries basis risk?
What market-maker economics are required for in-play sports contracts?
status_note: Organiser currently shows a 20:00 finish, but the final end time still needs confirming in event week.

title: PowerScale: Crypto × Meme × Anime × Social Opinion Market
access_note: Free; register on Luma, no approval needed
summary: Crowd-voted anime battles with cosplay creators, with Belief Market showing the results live on screen as the room divides. Hosted by Daniel Im of Belief Market. It sits at the opposite end of the spectrum from institutional clearing.
why: Worth a short visit to see prediction packaged as fandom or social engagement rather than finance. Look at what users predict, where rewards come from and how resolution works.
questions: What is the user predicting?
Where does reward/liquidity come from?
How does resolution work?
Do users describe the experience as trading, betting, fandom or gaming?
status_note: Times follow the organiser’s Luma page (18:00–21:00). The official TOKEN2049 Week listing, submitted by the same organiser, still shows 17:00–20:00. Check the Luma page on the day.

title: Prediction Market Traders Night
summary: Prediction-market traders night hosted by Moirai. The public description is currently thin.
why: Explicitly aimed at prediction-market traders. The guest list is not public, so how useful it is depends on who attends.
questions: Who is attending that actually makes markets or runs size?
status_note: Organiser Luma page (Moirai Research). Invite-only evening for people who trade, make markets in, research or build on prediction markets; 40 spots, confirmed individually.

title: Kalshi x Insilico Terminal: Asia Session @ TOKEN2049
summary: Curated evening for active traders, market makers, founders and investors across the Kalshi and Insilico communities.
why: The most trader-focused gathering of the week, aimed at the people whose capital and systems make the markets work.
questions: What annoys active traders most about event contracts today?
Where are books thin, feeds poor or settlement rules operationally awkward?
Which tools are you forced to build yourself?
status_note: Organiser event page (Luma).

title: Finality Forum @ TOKEN2049 SG
summary: Institutional digital-assets forum covering infrastructure, payments, RWA/tokenisation, agentic commerce, trading/liquidity and privacy.
why: Not a prediction-market conference, which is exactly why it's useful: a chance to ask institutional outsiders whether event contracts are showing up in their infrastructure and client requests.
questions: Do you see prediction markets showing up in client requests yet?
Which piece of the PM stack looks investable or useful from outside the category?
status_note: Organiser event page (Luma). Wintermute is also reported among its speakers.

venue: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark Observation Deck, 10 Bayfront Avenue
access_note: Separate ticket on Megatix; 18+ with photo ID; no guaranteed entry after 23:00
summary: Official closing party of TOKEN2049 week, headlined by Claptone and Crusy, with ANONM, Leon (FR), Milam and Mo-Shi. Smart casual; no re-entry after midnight.
why: Not prediction-market-specific: a general networking event for the whole conference.
questions: Who specifically do I need to see here?
status_note: Official TOKEN2049 site and TOKEN2049’s Megatix ticket page.

title: Global Onchain Summit Singapore 2026
summary: Afternoon onchain-finance summit powered by CoinGape. Kalshi’s Head of Institutional, Andy Ross, speaks on prediction markets, institutional adoption and next-generation market infrastructure.
why: A rare chance to hear Kalshi’s institutional lead on prediction markets before the main conference. Our sweep lists his session as “Prediction Markets: The Institutional Opportunity”.
questions: What is the first thing institutions ask for after they have basic access?
status_note: Organiser listing (Eventbrite / official site). Session title from our sweep; check the final agenda.

title: Predict, Watch, Verify: One-Minute Markets on Sui with PredictBay
summary: PredictBay CMO Zack Nelson presents one-minute prediction markets on Sui built on DeepBook Predict, at Sui Basecamp (7–8 Oct, alongside TOKEN2049).
why: A genuinely new prediction-market entrant that wasn’t in the original guide. By PredictBay’s own disclosure, paper trading is the live product and its DeepBook Predict integration is on testnet, so ask what’s real money today.
questions: What is live with real funds today, and when does DeepBook Predict reach mainnet?
How are one-minute markets resolved, and who supplies liquidity?

venue: Bit Digital Stage, Marina Bay Sands
summary: Official TOKEN2049 keynote from DWF Labs Managing Partner Andrei Grachev.
why: A market-maker and investor view of crypto markets. Adjacent context for prediction-market liquidity.

why: The strange and interesting intersection of prediction markets and AI training.
